title: Building major chords
summary: Stack a major 3rd and a perfect 5th from any root and you've got a major triad.

steps.title: Triads from intervals
steps.body: A major triad is built by stacking a major 3rd (4 semitones) and then a minor 3rd (3 semitones) above the root. From C: C + M3 = E, E + m3 = G. So C major = C E G. The same recipe works from any root.

steps.title: C major as three notes
steps.body: C E G shown on the fretboard. Notice the same three pitch classes show up everywhere -- there is no single 'C chord shape', just the same three notes voiced in different places.

steps.title: Major vs minor in one note
steps.body: If you flat the 3rd (M3 -> m3) the chord becomes minor. From C: C Eb G. That single note swap is the entire reason a chord sounds 'happy' or 'sad'. Try it on the fretboard -- pick any C major shape, lower the E by one fret, and listen.

steps.title: C major chord shape
steps.body: The standard open C: 5th fret-3 on string 5, fret-2 on string 4, open on string 3, fret-1 on string 2, open on string 1.

steps.title: G major chord shape
steps.body: Bigger reach but the recipe is the same: G B D, repeated across the strings.
